newsitem.title: UK: Mowlem places 49 pct of SGB unit.
newsitem.headline: Mowlem places 49 pct of SGB unit.

text.p: British construction group John Mowlem and Co Plc said on Thursday it would place 36.75 million shares at 150p each in its unit SGB Group Plc.
Mowlem said in a statement the placing of 49 percent of new and existing SGB shares, underwritten by Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, would raise 55.1 million stg and value the whole unit at 112.5 million.

Mowlem, which will retain 51 percent of SGB, said it would realise around 18.9 million stg from the placing but it would incur a charge of 37.1 million representing the reinstatement of goodwill previously written off when Mowlem bought SGB in 1986.
Mowlem said it expected the proposed flotation and listing on the London Stock Exchange to enhance group earnings in 1998.
Mowlem said the flotation would enable SGB to repay its debt to Mowlem and the redemption of the Mowlem Eurobond.
In addition, Mowlem said it would be able to participate in SGB's expected growth.
SGB is a supplier of access products and services, with operations in Britain, Europe, North America, the Middle East and the Asia Pacific region.
SGB employs 4,000 people and reported pre-tax profit of 13.9 million stg last year, with net assets of 68.1 million.
